summary: Find 100 NEW true-sponsorship gasless sources for ZERO (additive to Safe relay, which stays)

use_now.name: Beefy Finance — permissionless harvest() callFee
use_now.whoPays: The vault's harvested yield pays the caller. callFee starts at 50 = 0.5% of harvested rewards to whoever calls harvest(); a harvest(callFeeRecipient) overload exists so a contract can direct the fee.
use_now.apiOrContract: strategy.harvest() / harvest(address callFeeRecipient) — public, no registration
use_now.documentedLimit: No cap per address; competition is the limit (Beefy's own Cowllector bot harvests every vault ≥1×/24h and takes the profitable ones first)
use_now.why: This is ZERO's one proven earner (191 wins per the brief — the parent's measurement, not mine). Protocol pays the caller more than the call costs when sized right, which satisfies the sponsorship test. Docs quoted via search, not fetched. Honest risk: Beefy's own Cowllector is a well-capitalised competitor that explicitly targets the profitable harvests, so our margin is the tail it skips.
use_now.lane: LANE 1 — Keeper / automation networks that reimburse or sponsor gas

use_now.name: execution.market (Execution Market)
use_now.whoPays: The task PUBLISHER pays — they fund the USDC bounty and, on approve, one on-chain transaction settles the whole bounty; a Facilitator relayer broadcasts, so no participant needs native gas. Their reason: they want work done and pay 13% to the treasury for the rail.
use_now.apiOrContract: MCP tool em_register_as_executor; ERC-8128 wallet-signature auth + ERC-8004 on-chain identity (minted gaslessly via their Facilitator); USDC on Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Celo, Monad, SKALE; Solana live via pay.sh MPP 402 challenge
use_now.chains: Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Celo, Monad, SKALE, Solana
use_now.signupPath: Sign a registration request with the wallet key (ERC-8128) — no email, no captcha, no KYC, no human approval
use_now.documentedLimit: Fee is a flat 13% of the bounty (worker receives 87%), enforced inside the settlement transfer. No documented rate/volume cap.
use_now.why: Fetched https://execution.market and https://execution.market/llms.txt. Their own docs state 'trustless escrow, gasless payments, on-chain reputation', that registration requires 'an ERC-8128 wallet signature + an ERC-8004 identity (gasless, via Facilitator)', and that 'no gas is ever required from the executor'. Settlement evidence is documented, not claimed: changelog entry 'First real settle: task c7ae5eaa, $0.10, split verified on-chain (2026-08-08)'. That is a tiny amount — one $0.10 settle is proof the rail fires, NOT proof of a market. Caveat I am not hiding: publisher approval is a human/agent judgement call, so payment is not guaranteed by completion, and task liquidity was described elsewhere as low/mostly test tasks. Verdict is USE_NOW because registering and bidding costs us exactly nothing and the failure mode is wasted compute, not lost money.
use_now.lane: LANE 5 — venues that pay an agent where the gas is someone else's problem

use_now.name: agent402.tools (open x402 index + Smart Order Router)
use_now.whoPays: Buying agents pay per call in USDC; their facilitator broadcasts settlement. Listing in the index is free — the index operator bears its own crawl/infra cost to build a router it can monetize.
use_now.apiOrContract: POST /api/index/register (submit origin URL); GET /api/leaderboard, GET /api/stats, GET /api/status, GET /openapi.json; settlement address on Base 0xaBF4…a9D0
use_now.signupPath: POST your origin URL — 'we probe, you appear'. No account, no approval, no captcha.
use_now.documentedLimit: Undocumented rate limits; leaderboard snapshot is hourly
use_now.why: Fetched the site directly. This is the distribution half of the x402 shape: we stand up a paid endpoint, POST the URL, and get crawled into a router that agents buy through. Ranking is by REAL settled USDC, not self-reported — the leaderboard showed a live seller at $21,788.08 settled, which is the strongest third-party settlement evidence I found in this lane. It pays us nothing by itself; it is the shelf, not the product. USE_NOW because it is a zero-cost, zero-human listing that turns any x402 endpoint we ship into something discoverable by paying agents.
use_now.lane: LANE 5 — venues that pay an agent where the gas is someone else's problem

use_now.name: x402 protocol (seller side, any non-CDP facilitator)
use_now.whoPays: The BUYER's payment carries settlement: the buyer signs an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization (or ERC-2612 permit) off-chain, and the FACILITATOR broadcasts the transaction. The seller (us) never touches native gas.
use_now.apiOrContract: HTTP 402 challenge + X-PAYMENT header; facilitator /verify and /settle endpoints; EIP-3009 (USDC everywhere) or ERC-2612
use_now.chains: Base primarily (>90% of x402 traffic), plus Solana, Stellar, Algorand, 170+ EVM via thirdweb
use_now.signupPath: None. Serve a 402 with a payTo address and a /.well-known/x402.json manifest. No account anywhere in the protocol.
use_now.documentedLimit: Protocol imposes none; individual facilitators set fees (0% Coinbase, 1.5% Stripe, 1–2% Nevermined)
use_now.why: Fetched the spec README. It states the design principle that 'the client/server should not need to think about gas, rpc, etc.' and that a resource server may settle by POSTing the payload to a facilitator's /settle endpoint instead of touching a chain. MEASURED vs INFERRED, plainly: I verified from the spec that the seller does not broadcast; I am INFERRING (not measuring) that the facilitator operator absorbs the gas rather than netting it out of proceeds — that varies per facilitator and must be re-checked against whichever one we pick. This is the lane's core mechanic rather than a venue: it is the only rail found where a permanently $0 wallet can accrue USDC with no counterparty relationship, no signup, and no human. Coinbase CDP is banned for us, so the facilitator must be Cloudflare, thirdweb, xpay.sh, Nevermined, or self-hosted.
use_now.lane: LANE 5 — venues that pay an agent where the gas is someone else's problem

promising: Gelato Relay — callWithSyncFee — The TARGET CONTRACT pays Gelato's relay fee, synchronously, out of tokens it already holds or just earned in that same call. ZERO never needs native gas — Gelato's executor submits the transaction.
Convex Finance — Booster.earmarkRewards(pid) — Convex's harvested CRV pays the caller. callIncentive = crvBalance * earmarkIncentive / FEE_DENOMINATOR, transferred to msg.sender.
Aura Finance — Booster.earmarkRewards(pid) — Aura's harvested BAL pays the caller; Booster.earmarkIncentive is paid as a percentage to whoever calls earmarkRewards on behalf of Aura.

Aerodrome / Velodrome — Relay AutoCompounder public caller reward — The Relay's own compounded VELO/AERO pays the caller: public callers receive the minimum of (a) 1% of the VELO converted from swaps or (b) a constant VELO reward set by the team.

Synthetix v3 — perps order settlement keeper — The TRADER pays: minKeeperFee is a static sUSD amount paid to whoever settles the order, funded from the trader's order fees. Stale-order cancellation pays the same minKeeperFee.

Liquity V2 (BOLD) — permissionless liquidation — The liquidated borrower's collateral pays: the liquidator receives compensation for the effective gas costs PLUS a margin. Batching multiple liquidatable Troves in one call is supported.

Superfluid — Sentinel (Pleb / Pirate) stream liquidation — The insolvent STREAM SENDER's buffer deposit pays the liquidator. Docs explicitly state anyone can run a Pleb or Pirate sentinel with NO capital requirements.

Olas (Autonolas) Mech Marketplace — The REQUESTING AGENT pays: fees for delivering a task are collected by the Mech Marketplace into a balance tracker and paid out to the delivering Mech. Crypto-native, API-key-free micropayments — the original 2023 mechs existed so agents could buy AI inference without an API key.
Third-party dApps sponsoring via Gelato 1Balance (us as the caller) — The sponsoring project, out of its own 1Balance USDC. It is never billed back to the caller.

Plasma (XPL) protocol-level zero-fee USDT paymaster — The Plasma Foundation — it funds the paymaster and covers gas at the moment of sponsorship, not reimbursed after the fact. Genuinely never billed to the user.

Jupiter — JupiterZ (RFQ) and Ultra gasless — Two different answers, and the difference matters: Ultra gasless deducts gas from the swap output (user pays). JupiterZ RFQ — the MARKET MAKER pays network and priority fees, and Jupiter's own gas wallet pays the rent to create the taker's output token account
Polymarket Relayer — Polymarket's own relayer infrastructure pays 100% of Polygon gas — wallet deployment, USDC approvals, trades and withdrawals — and does not bill it back to the trader
Hyperliquid signed actions — Nobody — the protocol carries the cost architecturally. Orders and cancels are consensus-level signed actions, so there is no gas to bear
Internet Computer reverse gas model — The canister's developer, who prefunds it with cycles. Users never obtain tokens, configure wallets, or pay for calls
Gelato Relay sponsoredCall (third-party-funded dapps) — The integrating dapp, out of its prefunded Gelato 1Balance — never billed back to the end user

SKALE zero-gas mainnet chains (Europa / Calypso / Nebula) — The sChain owner. sFUEL is pre-minted in massive surplus, is explicitly valueless, and is recycled on-chain — it 'never runs out'. Nobody bills the transacting address, ever.

SKALE gasless Proof-of-Work (mineGasForTransaction) — Nobody. The client burns local CPU to derive a magic gasPrice; validators verify the work instead of debiting a balance. Cost is our own electricity, which we already pay.

Internet Computer — reverse gas model — The canister (contract) owner. Canisters are pre-loaded with cycles and burn them to serve inbound calls; the calling identity pays nothing and needs no token, no account, and no balance.
Sonic Fee Monetization (FeeM) — Sonic's fee pool, funded by OUR app's users. Registered contracts receive up to 90% of the gas fees third parties spend interacting with them.

Cloudflare Monetization Gateway — The crawling/calling AI agent pays per resource in stablecoins over x402; Cloudflare's edge verifies before forwarding to origin. Cloudflare bears the verification infrastructure because it wants to own the agent-payment toll booth.

thirdweb x402 (server / seller SDK) — Buyer signs and pays; thirdweb's facilitator service settles onchain. AMBIGUOUS: their docs say the facilitator 'handles settling the payment onchain using your own server wallet', which may mean OUR wallet broadcasts and therefore needs gas.

xpay.sh (independent x402 facilitator + MCP monetization) — Calling agents pay per invocation in USDC on Base; xpay operates the proxy/facilitator and settles. Their reason: they take a cut of the flow they route.

SKALE zero-gas chains + sFUEL PoW faucet — The SKALE chain operator / chain economics. sFUEL is an intentionally valueless, unpurchasable gas token distributed free by the chain operator, dApps, or a public faucet — validators are paid by the network, not by transactors.

Nostr NIP-90 Data Vending Machines — The requesting customer pays a Lightning bolt11 invoice or zap. There is no blockchain gas in the flow at all — Lightning routing fees are millisats and borne by the payer.

Apify x402 agentic payments (we are already an Apify seller) — The calling agent — 'the client sends a payment signature with an allowance instead of a final amount', Apify runs the Actor and charges actual usage in USDC on Base (eip155:8453). Apify operates the rail and already pays developers out.
rejected: Chainlink Automation (as a customer): Answers the lane's explicit question with a clean no: an unregistered wallet CANNOT perform Chainlink jobs and be paid — execution is done by the DON's nodes, which do not compete with each other, and the LINK comes from the upkeep owner. This makes us the payer with a premium on top. Exactly the 'the user eventually pays' shape the brief says to reject. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

PowerPool PowerAgent: The economics are actually good — gas compensated even on failure is unusually generous — but it is stake-gated. A $0 wallet cannot buy CVP, and the reward is explicitly proportional to stake, so even a token entry earns the worst jobs. Fails the zero-balance test at the door, not at the margin. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

Olas / Autonolas — Proof-of-Active-Agent staking: Marketing calls the Autonomous Keeper Service 'permissionless', and joining is — but EARNING is stake-gated by Proof-of-Active-Agent. That gap between 'anyone may participate' and 'anyone gets paid' is the single most common trap in this lane and this is the cleanest example of it. Docs quoted via search, not fetched. (The Mech Marketplace, listed separately above, is the non-staked part of Olas and is the part worth pursuing.)

OpenZeppelin Defender (Relayers + Autotasks): Double-dead. Even when alive it was infrastructure we fund, not sponsorship — the docs are explicit that YOU fund the relayer. But it is now also past its shutdown date and closed to new signups over a year ago, so any plan or blog post recommending it is stale. Flagging this loudly because Defender appears in most 'gasless keeper' tutorials and would otherwise waste a session. Sunset FAQ quoted via search, not fetched.

Gelato Web3 Functions / Automate (as task creator): FETCHED the pricing page and it kills a widely-repeated belief: there is NO free tier for Gelato Web3 Functions, the entry price is $99/month. Search snippets elsewhere claim 'free tier limits' exist — the actual pricing table contradicts them, which is exactly why this needed fetching. Rejected as an automation host. Note this rejects Gelato-as-scheduler ONLY; Gelato Relay callWithSyncFee (first entry) is a different product and still stands.

Sky (MakerDAO) Keeper Network: Onboarding is a governance proposal, i.e. humans voting — instant fail on the machine-only rule. Worse, it is contracting: Dewiz was asked to deactivate the GELATO lane, deactivate the KEEP3R lane, and disable both NetworkPaymentAdapter claim paths. That is a leading indicator that keeper-network demand from the largest historical buyer is being withdrawn, which discounts Keep3r's future value too. Sky forum + MIP quoted via search, not fetched.

Across Protocol — permissionless relayer: Textbook 'permissionless but not free': a relayer FRONTS the user's full bridged amount on the destination chain out of its own inventory and waits for reimbursement. The fee even names capital-at-risk as a compensated cost, which is an admission that capital is the entry fee. $0 inventory means zero fills, permanently. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

Hyperlane — permissionless relayer: 'Anyone can run one' is true and irrelevant — income requires senders to configure YOU as their relayer, which is a business-development problem, not a machine problem, and it is precisely the distribution lever we structurally do not have. Plus the relayer fronts destination gas. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

Compound v3 (Comet) — absorb(): Deliberately designed NOT to be a race — Compound's own docs say absorb pays only gas so there is no incentive to compete. The value sits in buyCollateral, which requires base-asset capital to buy the seized collateral at a discount. So: the free half pays nothing and the paying half needs money we don't have. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

Curve gauge — kick() / user_checkpoint: Included as a negative result so it isn't re-investigated: this is one of the most-cited 'permissionless keeper action' examples in DeFi writeups and it pays exactly zero. It is a governance hygiene function, not a bounty. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

Pyth Network — permissionless updatePriceFeeds: Perfect illustration of the brief's warning: 'permissionless' here means anyone may PAY to update, the opposite of getting paid. Value only appears if you bundle the update with a downstream action that pays (a Synthetix settlement, a liquidation) — in which case the payer is that protocol, not Pyth. Same applies to RedStone's pull model. Docs quoted via search, not fetched.

ERC-4337 public paymasters (Alchemy, Openfort, and similar): Rejected on both tests. Sponsorship: an app sponsors ITS users to acquire them — we are nobody's user-acquisition target, so there is no reason for any of them to bear our keeper gas. Machine-only: mainnet policies need a dashboard account and a payment method. Coinbase's paymaster is separately hard-banned. Reviews quoted via search, not fetched.

Brahma Console: Named in the brief so it gets a verdict rather than silence: Brahma is a cockpit, not an income source. It makes an already-funded operator more efficient; it cannot expand a zero balance because there is no third party in the loop with a reason to pay. INFERRED from product positioning — I did not fetch their docs, and nothing found suggested a sponsorship program that would change this.

Candide ERC-20 token paymaster (pay gas in USDC/DAI/USDT): VERIFIED: returned USDC, DAI, USDT and USDS with live exchangeRate fields. This is precisely the gas-denomination trap the brief bans — paying in USDC instead of ETH is not free gas, and with a $0.00 balance we have no stablecoins to pay with either. Rejected on the stated rule.

Pimlico sponsorship via public endpoint: VERIFIED refusal: a fully-formed unauthenticated pm_sponsorUserOperation returned error -32601 'Sponsorship policy ID is required for this API key'. The public endpoint deliberately excludes sponsorship. Clean, unambiguous no.

Pimlico free tier / pay-as-you-go: FETCHED the pricing docs directly. The free tier sponsors testnet gas only and mainnet access requires a card on file — two independent disqualifiers (no true sponsorship, and a card we will never add). The canonical example of the testnet-free/mainnet-paid pattern.

Alchemy Gas Manager: FETCHED the official FAQ, which states mainnet base limit is literally N/A on the free tier while testnet sponsorship is unlimited. Marketing copy elsewhere advertises '$50/mo free sponsored gas' without saying testnet-only — a genuinely misleading claim I would have repeated had I not read the docs.

ZeroDev paymaster: INFERRING from docs and pricing page (not endpoint-tested). The billing model is stated plainly: they front, then charge a card. A card is a hard immovable for us and there is no mainnet free allowance.
thirdweb account abstraction: INFERRING from their docs. Card required for mainnet, a paid subscription floor, and a 10% premium on top of gas. Fails machine-only and fails who-pays simultaneously.

Biconomy paymaster / Gas Tank: INFERRING from docs. The model is explicitly a prepaid tank we must fill. Separately VERIFIED that Biconomy's long-circulated public demo bundler key (nJPK7B3ru.dd7f...) is dead — both v2 and v3 paths returned empty responses on Base.
Particle Network paymaster: INFERRING from docs. Testnet is genuinely free and auto-sponsored, but mainnet needs a USDT deposit plus a webhook we would have to host. No mainnet free tier exists.

Openfort gas sponsorship: INFERRING from docs. Slightly better than peers in that no card is demanded up front, but mainnet still runs off a balance we would have to fund. Free credits are testnet-scoped.

Etherspot Arka paymaster + Skandha bundler (hosted): VERIFIED by curl: rpc.etherspot.io/v2/8453 returned '{"message":"Api key not found, visit https://etherspot.fyi for more information"}'. Confirms a dashboard signup a machine cannot complete, and the free tier is testnet-only regardless. Arka is good open-source software but the hosted rail is closed to us.

Stackup bundler + paymaster: VERIFIED dead: api.stackup.sh/v1/node/8453 returned an empty response. Repository archived October 2024 and read-only; Stackup shut down its bundler and paymaster to pivot. Historic 'free node service on Ethereum mainnet' posts still circulate and are stale. Self-hosting the archived Go bundler remains possible but pays no gas.

Gelato Relay 1Balance (as our own account): INFERRING from docs (the 1Balance docs URL 404'd; sourced from the pricing page and Safe/thirdweb integration guides). For ZERO to run its own 1Balance we must deposit stablecoins we do not have, and mainnet sponsorship is not subsidised — only testnet runs are.

Status Network 'gasless L2': TRAP — flagging loudly. Marketing site, blog and press releases still describe this as the first gasless L2 at scale, but VERIFIED that docs.status.network returns an archived 404 stating 'Status Network has merged into Linea. The content here is obsolete and kept online for archival purposes only.' Both RPC hosts I probed returned nothing. Search results alone would have produced a confident false positive here. Also would have failed anyway: free throughput required a positive Karma balance bought with capital.

Zyfi Gas Grants Program: FETCHED the page. This is exactly the 'ecosystem grant page that is really a contact form' the brief said to reject and name. It is a Google Form gated on human approval, and the eligibility floor (100 daily users, 500 daily txs) is unreachable for us regardless. The money is real; the door is human-only. Double disqualification.

OpenZeppelin Defender Relayer: INFERRING from docs. Fails twice: we fund the relayer ourselves (zero sponsorship), and the Defender platform is being retired on 1 July 2026. Do not build on it. The open-sourced Relayer/Monitor code survives but is self-hosted and still needs our own gas.

Self-hostable bundlers (eth-infinitism, Rundler, Voltaire, Skandha, Silius, Alto, Transeptor): Listed for completeness because these are frequently miscited as a free-gas option. They are free SOFTWARE with zero signup, which is real, but running one requires a funded signer EOA — it is a gas SINK, not a source. (The bundlers.erc4337.io compliance table failed to load its results when I fetched it, so I am not reporting per-bundler scores.)

Circle Paymaster: Rejected on the brief's explicit standing rule: paying gas in USDC instead of ETH is gas denomination, not sponsorship. It cannot expand a zero balance — and we hold no USDC to denominate in. Noted here only so it is not re-proposed later.

1inch Fusion / Fusion+: HARD REJECT on the machine-only rule, and this is the cleanest kill in the lane. The Fusion SDK's authKey comes only from the 1inch Business portal, and obtaining it requires completing a KYC/KYB procedure — a human identity verification step ZERO structurally cannot pass and that we are forbidden to hand to Anthony. The gasless mechanics are excellent and irrelevant to us. INFERRED from search results, not a fetched docs page — but the KYC claim appeared consistently and the direction of the error would only make it worse, not better. Do not spend more time here; use CoW or Velora instead.

Kaia Fee Delegation Service: REJECT on two independent grounds, both FETCHED from Kaia's own docs. First, machine-only fails hard: access is a Google Form plus manual human configuration by the Kaia team — this is the 'ecosystem page that is really a contact form' pattern the brief says to call out. Second, even past the gate it is not sponsorship: the docs describe checking whether YOUR DApp's balance is sufficient and contacting the team to deposit more, i.e. we fund it. Kaia's protocol-level fee delegation (two-signature transactions) is genuinely elegant tech and worth knowing exists, but the public service in front of it is closed to us.

Ronin Waypoint gas sponsorship: REJECT on machine-only, verified by FETCHING Sky Mavis's docs. The sponsorship itself is real and unreimbursed — Ronin's own funds pay — but access runs through Ronin Waypoint, which is a social-login account system, and any meaningful allowance requires 'contact your Ronin point of contact to apply', with a template naming contract addresses and dates. Two human gates. The five free transactions per new user is also exactly the kind of per-account allowance that only scales by creating accounts, which is the abuse pattern that gets identities nuked. Documented here so nobody re-researches it.

Immutable zkEVM / Passport gas sponsorship: REJECT twice over. Machine-only fails at Passport's social login. And the sponsorship is explicitly billed onward — Immutable's own wording is that it recoups from the counterparty, at roughly $500-$1,000 per 100,000 users. If we were ever the studio, we would be the one paying. The only scenario where this is free to us is transacting inside someone else's game as a player, which requires the login we cannot do. Closed.

AVNU Paymaster (Starknet): REJECT for our purposes despite being good infrastructure. Two disqualifiers: (1) it is a paymaster we would have to FUND, so it is our money, not a third party's — the gas-abstraction mode is literally the 'pay in another token' pattern the brief says to reject; (2) the killer detail is that AVNU does not sponsor ACCOUNT DEPLOYMENT — a fresh Starknet wallet must pay STRK to exist before any sponsorship applies, which is precisely the wall a $0.00 agent hits first. INFERRING from search summaries. Noted so the account-deployment trap is on record for any future Starknet idea.

Aptos sponsored transactions (fee payer) + Gas Station Credits: REJECT. The fee-payer standard itself is a primitive, not a source — it lets SOMEONE pay for us but does not produce that someone. The only genuine third-party money here is Aptos Foundation Gas Station Credits, and that runs through aptosnetwork.com/grants, i.e. a grant application with human review. That is the 'grant page that is really a contact form' pattern, and it fails machine-only. Recording the primitive because the simulation trick (feePayerAddress 0x0 to skip gas checks) is genuinely useful if we ever need to dry-run Aptos transactions for free.

Blast gas revenue share: REJECT, and the reason is not the mechanism — it is the venue. Same deployer-needs-traffic problem as Mode and Sonic, but with the added issue that Blast's activity collapsed after its points campaign ended, so the revenue being shared is a share of near-nothing. Building on a chain for its rebate when the chain has no users is the fee-rebate version of building before validating. Listed so it is documented as considered and killed rather than quietly missing.

World Chain gas allowance for verified humans: REJECT, and it is the most absolute rejection in the lane — the eligibility criterion is literally proof that you are NOT a machine, verified by iris scan at a physical Orb. There is no workaround, and attempting one would be identity fraud. Additionally note the stated economic design: World Chain intends to fund human users' free gas from fees charged to BOTS. We are the ones they plan to bill. Documented permanently so nobody revisits World Chain as a gasless option.

Octane (Solana gasless relayer): REJECT as a source, though it is good software. Running it ourselves means WE are the sponsor — the docs are explicit that you must manage the fee payer keypair, top it up with SOL, and regularly swap accepted tokens back to SOL. That is us paying, plus operational overhead. And using someone else's Octane node means paying them in SPL tokens, which is gas denomination, not free gas. Also note the deployment story assumes Vercel, which is hard-banned for us anyway. Use JupiterZ instead for Solana — there the market maker genuinely eats the fee.

Coinbase CDP Paymaster / Base Paymaster: REJECT twice: it is on our hard-banned list (Coinbase CDP / Paymaster / AgentKit, past-due account), and independently it fails the sponsorship test because the app funds it and gets billed — it is our money with extra steps. Recorded here only because Base Paymaster dominates every search result for gasless-on-Base and will keep resurfacing in future sweeps; this entry exists so the next agent stops rather than re-researching it. Same disposition applies to Zora's gasless minting, which appears in the same searches and is also on the banned list.

SKALE Base Mainnet (CREDIT / Compute Credits model): This is SKALE's newer paid model and the direction the network is moving. It is gas re-denominated as prepaid credits — exactly the 'you pay in something else' pattern we reject. Also note PoW is disabled by default on credit chains, so it does not rescue this. Use the older Ethereum-connected zero-gas chains instead.

Safe relayer — full chain re-enumeration (closing the question): MEASURED, not remembered. I probed 49 chain IDs against the Safe client-gateway relay endpoint with a browser UA. Exactly six return {"remaining":5,"limit":5}: 10, 100, 130, 137, 8453, 42161 — identical to what we already had. Seventeen return {"message":"No relayer defined","statusCode":403}: 1, 146, 204, 324, 480, 999, 5000, 10200, 42220, 43114, 57073, 59144, 80094, 84532, 534352, 1313161554, 11155111. Twenty-six are not onboarded to Safe at all (404): 25, 30, 122, 169, 250, 252, 288, 291, 360, 690, 1088, 1101, 1116, 1135, 1284, 1329, 1750, 1868, 2020, 2741, 7000, 33139, 34443, 42170, 53456, 55244, 60808, 81457, 421614. Verdict REJECT means 'no NEW capability here' — the six known chains still work. Stop searching this avenue.

Blast gas fee revenue share: Honest read: on our OWN transactions this is a partial refund of money we already spent, so it cannot expand a zero balance — 'who ultimately pays?' is still us, minus a discount. It only becomes true sponsorship on volume from OTHER users, at which point Sonic's 90% (above) is a strictly better version of the same idea. Listed so it is not re-discovered as a new lead. Inferred from docs.

Mode Sequencer Fee Sharing (SFS): Same shape as Blast but at 25%, which is strictly worse than the gas we spend — it cannot fund anything from zero, and monthly claiming itself costs gas. Registration mints an NFT (on-chain, machine-doable), so the mechanics are fine; the economics are not. Inferred from docs.

Kaia Fee Delegation Service: Double disqualification. (1) Access is a Google Form — 'the Kaia team communicates and configures the Dapp into FeeDelegationServer... once the Google form is submitted' — that is a human approval step. (2) Even after approval the balance is ours. Kaia's native fee-delegation transaction types (FEE_DELEGATED_*) are a genuinely elegant protocol feature, but the protocol only lets a fee payer exist; it does not supply one.

vechain.energy fee delegation (VIP-191 sponsor endpoint): The free/open sponsorship is explicitly testnet-only ('open sponsorship on all TestNet transactions to help new applications start faster'). The mainnet endpoint https://sponsor.vechain.energy/by/{PROJECT_ID} draws on a VTHO balance we deposit. Also needs an account + project created on their dashboard. Real product, wrong side of the payment arrow. Testnet-only for us.

Shinami Gas Station (Aptos free period): Textbook example of the trap this lane exists to catch: marketed as a free gas station, but the free part is the middleman's markup, not the gas. The chain fee still comes out of our funded sponsor account. Dashboard signup also required.

Sui — Enoki (Mysten Labs) sponsored transactions: Sui's sponsored-transaction primitive (separate gas owner from sender) is excellent engineering, and Enoki/Shinami/Ignitia all productise it — but every one of them is a pipe from OUR wallet to the validator. The 'free tier' is a MAU allowance on the service, which people routinely misread as free gas. Also requires a developer portal account.

Immutable zkEVM gas sponsorship: MEASURED: eth_gasPrice on https://rpc.immutable.com returned 0x28fa6ae31 (~11 gwei) — this is not a zero-gas chain; the 'gas-free' claim is a relayer on top. Sponsorship only applies to transactions signed by an Immutable Passport wallet (a hosted consumer wallet with social/email onboarding), not a raw EOA, and configuration lives behind a Developer Hub account. Cost is quoted at $500–$1,000 per 100k users — i.e. someone is definitely paying, and it would be us.

XION (Burnt) treasury contracts / Cosmos feegrant: XION markets itself as 'the chainless/gasless chain' and the on-chain OAuth-like grant flow is genuinely well designed, but the granter account is funded by the app. I searched specifically for a PUBLIC feegrant granter — a chain-run account that grants allowances to any address on request — and found none on XION or elsewhere in Cosmos. If one ever appears it would be a true match for this lane.

Abstract — native AA paymasters: MEASURED: eth_gasPrice on https://api.mainnet.abs.xyz returned 0x2b275d0 (~45 mwei) — cheap, not free. Abstract inherits ZKsync's native paymaster support, which means anyone CAN sponsor, not that anyone DOES. I found no chain-run public paymaster open to arbitrary contracts, and no documented Abstract program that pays a stranger's gas.

Sophon — SOPH paymaster: MEASURED: eth_gasPrice on https://rpc.sophon.xyz returned 0x9184e72a000 (10 gwei in SOPH) — transactions are not free at the protocol level. The widely repeated 'Sophon is gasless' line reduces to 'ZKsync paymasters exist and some apps use them'. Any blanket Sophon-pays-everyone program would be a partner deal, i.e. a human conversation.

Lens Chain sponsorships: MEASURED: eth_gasPrice on https://rpc.lens.xyz returned 0xa52ce0b5 (~2.8 gwei). Lens's sponsorship primitive is app-funded and its API sits behind app-level auth. Included because 'Lens is gasless' is a persistent claim worth having a measurement against.

Flow — sponsored-transaction EVM gateway: MEASURED: the public endpoints https://mainnet.evm.nodes.onflow.org and https://testnet.evm.nodes.onflow.org both returned eth_gasPrice = 0x12abb24b80 (~80 gwei) — NOT zero. So there is no free public gasless Flow RPC; the zero-gas-price gateway is one we would run and fund ourselves. Flow's Cadence fee-payer role is genuinely first-class (payer is a separate signer), which is why this keeps showing up in 'gasless chain' lists — but the money is still ours.

Starknet — AVNU Paymaster: Both AVNU modes fail the who-ultimately-pays test: either we prepay credits or the user is debited an equivalent in USDC (the exact Circle-Paymaster pattern already banned in this brief). Free tier exists but is explicitly for testing on testnet, and an x-paymaster-api-key from a dashboard is required for mainnet.

Etherspot Arka Paymaster: Genuinely useful open-source infrastructure across Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, Avalanche, Gnosis, BNB, Rootstock, Flare, Fuse and Mantle for EntryPoint v0.7 — and entirely irrelevant to a zero balance, because it validates eligibility and then spends OUR deposit. Recorded so it is not mistaken for free gas on a future sweep.

Gelato Relay / 1Balance: The engine behind Safe's relayer, and the reason Safe's six chains work — but bought directly it is a prepaid account, not sponsorship. The only free path documented is depositing testnet ETH for testnet relaying. Login is wallet-based (machine-friendly), which is the one point in its favour if we ever have money.

BNB Chain Gas Grants: Real money from a real third party, but gated three ways: an application form, a requirement of average DAU > 100 over the preceding 30 days, and at least one security audit. Every one of those is a human step, and the DAU bar is a chicken-and-egg we cannot clear from zero. This is precisely the 'ecosystem grant page that is really a contact form' category the brief says to reject and say so.

ArbiFuel (Arbitrum gas coverage): EXPIRED. The program is documented as covering gas fees for eligible teams only until 31 January 2026 — it is now August 2026. Listed so nobody re-finds it in a stale blog roundup and treats it as live. Application-based in any case.

Base Builder Grants (Gitcoin): Retroactive ETH that could offset gas, but it is nominated/reviewed by humans and identity-linked (Talent/Gitcoin profile, typically GitHub-connected). Fails machine-only outright, and it pays after the fact so it cannot fund the first transaction. Note it is also on our default chain, so if Anthony ever wants a human-in-the-loop rail this is the least bad one — but it is not a source for this lane.

Optimism Superchain Faucet: Two disqualifiers. It is TESTNET ETH only (OP Sepolia, Base Sepolia, Mode Sepolia, Zora Sepolia etc.), not mainnet — the 'up to 1 ETH' figure that circulates is testnet. And larger drips require on-chain identity: World ID, an EAS attestation, an Optimist NFT (earned via a Coinbase Wallet quest), or a Gitcoin Passport score > 25. All human. Recording this kills a recurring false lead.

World Chain free gas allowance: Structurally the exact inverse of what we need: the entire mechanism is designed to give free gas to PROVEN HUMANS and deny it to machines. Orb verification is a physical, in-person biometric step. Also note Safe has no relayer on chain 480 (measured 403 'No relayer defined'). Dead end by design, permanently.

Feeless L1s without programmability (Nano / IOTA): Two reasons, one measured. (1) Feeless does not mean actionable from zero: a Nano account with no XNO can receive but cannot originate value, and there is no contract layer to do anything useful with. (2) MEASURED: IOTA's EVM layer is NOT feeless — eth_gasPrice on https://json-rpc.evm.iotaledger.net returned 0x2540be400 (10 gwei). The 'feeless IOTA' claim applies to L1 only, and IOTA 2.0 gates L1 throughput behind Mana anyway. Both fail as execution venues.

Etherlink (Tezos L2): MEASURED: eth_gasPrice on https://node.mainnet.etherlink.com returned 0x3b9aca00 (1 gwei) in XTZ. Cheap, EVM, no permission needed — but there is no free path in, and Safe has no relayer there. Included as a measured negative because 'near-zero gas L2' lists keep surfacing it as if near-zero were zero. Near-zero times a zero balance is still zero.

Broad zero-gas-price sweep across 25+ mainnets (measured negative): To stop this question being re-asked: I POSTed eth_gasPrice to the public RPC of every plausible 'free gas' mainnet and NONE returned zero. Base 0x5b8d80 · Blast 0xf433c · Mode 0xf433e · B3 0xf433c · Xai 0x5f5e100 · Vana 0x236df02 · Abstract 0x2b275d0 · Lens 0xa52ce0b5 · Immutable 0x28fa6ae31 · Etherlink 0x3b9aca00 · IOTA EVM 0x2540be400 · Flow EVM 0x12abb24b80 · Kaia 0x66720b300 · Sonic 0xcce416600 · Degen 0x1bf08eb000 · ApeChain 0x17acc3c940 · Fuse 0x4a817c800 · Shardeum 0x82f9bed8b18e7. Only the SKALE chains sit at the floor (0x186a0 = 100,000 wei on a valueless token). CONCLUSION: SKALE is not merely the best option in this lane — measured against 25 candidates it is the only structurally zero-cost EVM mainnet execution venue that exists. Everything else in Lane 4 is someone agreeing to pay, and the only ones who agree without a form are foundations paying their own consumer wallets' users.

Masumi Network (Cardano agent registry + escrow): Rejected on the lane's own test: to be findable we must mint an on-chain registration NFT, which costs ADA we do not have and cannot obtain without a human funding us. It also drags in a whole new chain and a new asset we would have to off-ramp. Good architecture, wrong side of the gas line for a zero balance.

Virtuals Protocol ACP (Agent Commerce Protocol): REJECT on the machine-only rule, and it is not close: the docs state 'all agent graduation requests will undergo manual review by the team', and the default currency must be whitelisted for your wallet. That is a human approval gate plus a whitelist gate. The escrow economics are genuinely good (80% to the provider, buyer's escrow carries settlement), so if the manual review is ever removed this flips to PROMISING — but today it fails the one constraint that defines this experiment.

Circle Agent Services Marketplace: Fetched the Circle post. The payment mechanics are exactly right and Circle confirms the gasless framing, but the listing path is a Google Form plus approval by Circle, which is a human gate with a human on the other end deciding. REJECT as a machine-only venue. Worth noting the useful fact buried in it: Circle Gateway's batched settlement is another genuine 'somebody else eats the gas' mechanism, distinct from Circle Paymaster which does the opposite.

Skyfire (KYAPay): REJECT, decisively. 'Know Your Agent' is KYC wearing a different hat — the docs describe attaching a real-world human or business identity to every agent you control, plus a multi-stage provider review. That is the exact opposite of zero-humans-ever, and it would drag Anthony into an identity process for a speculative rail. Not worth revisiting.

UMA Optimistic Oracle / Polymarket proposing: REJECT on capital, not on principle. The economics are absurd for us regardless of gas: $750 at risk to earn $2, and a wrong dispute forfeits the entire bond. This is the archetype of the whole rejected category — 'the protocol pays the caller' only ever means 'the caller fronts money and is repaid', which a $0 wallet can never enter. Naming it so nobody re-proposes it.

Keep3r Network: REJECT despite the tempting 'no funds required to become a keeper' line — that is about bonding, not about execution. Every job call is a transaction the keeper broadcasts and pays for, then gets reimbursed with a premium. At a $0 balance there is no call zero to bootstrap from, and many jobs additionally filter on bond size or earnings history we do not have. Same failure as UMA: reimbursement is not sponsorship.

Ocean Protocol Predictoor: REJECT. It requires per-epoch staking and per-epoch transactions from our own wallet — cost before revenue, which is exactly what we cannot do. Also worth stating plainly for scale: a 500 USDC/week pool split across every predictoor in the world is not a path to $7.23/day for us, even if we could fund it.

poidh (pics or it didn't happen): REJECT: claiming requires the claimant to mint an on-chain claim, so ZERO would have to pay gas before it could ever be paid. Bounty acceptance is also a poster's discretionary vote, so even a funded attempt is unpaid work with a coin-flip. Searched specifically for a gas-sponsored claim path and found none.

Circle Paymaster: Listing this REJECT explicitly because it surfaced in nearly every search in this lane and is constantly mis-sold as 'gasless'. It is gas DENOMINATION, not sponsorship: we pay gas plus 10%, in USDC. It cannot expand a zero balance — it can only shrink a non-zero one faster. Same category as the banned Coinbase paymaster model. If it ever gets proposed again, this entry is the answer.
laneSummaries:
LANE 1 — Keeper / automation networks that reimburse or sponsor gas: CENTRAL FINDING, and it is bad news dressed honestly: almost every "gas reimbursed" keeper network reimburses POST-HOC. The keeper submits the transaction from its own wallet, pays native gas at block time, and is paid back afterwards in KP3R / CVP / ETH / sUSD. A wallet at $0.00 cannot enter ANY of those — reimbursement is a margin business, not a bootstrap. Only two shapes actually pass the "somebody else bears the cost" test in this lane: (a) a relayer submits for us and takes its fee out of the reward the call itself produced — Gelato Relay `callWithSyncFee` is the only such rail I found that we do not already have (Safe's relayer excluded per brief); (b) an already-funded submission path we control, which is presumably how ZERO's 191 Beefy wins happened — I did NOT verify ZERO's actual submission mechanism and the parent should treat "we can already submit somehow" as the load-bearing unknown for this whole lane. Every PROMISING entry below is really "PROMISING *conditional on* an existing zero-cost submission path"; the caller-fee economics are real and permissionless, the gas fronting is the blocker.

SECOND FINDING: the dedicated keeper *networks* are the worst of the set. PowerPool requires a CVP stake. Olas requires an OLAS stake. Chainlink Automation makes us the payer, not the earner (execution is by the DON). OpenZeppelin Defender is DEAD — new signups disabled 2025-06-30, full shutdown 2026-07-01, i.e. already past. Gelato Web3 Functions has NO free tier (Pro $99/mo). Sky/Maker is actively DEACTIVATING its Gelato and Keep3r lanes, which shrinks Keep3r's paying demand. The money is not in the keeper networks — it is in individual protocols' permissionless caller-fee functions (Beefy, Convex/Aura earmark, Aerodrome Relay autocompounder, Synthetix settlement, Liquity liquidation), which need no registration, no stake, and no signup at all.

EVIDENCE HONESTY: I directly FETCHED only three sources (Gelato non-sponsored-calls, Keep3r keepers page, Gelato pricing page) — those are marked verified:true. Everything else is a docs-site quote returned through search, not a page I pulled myself; those are verified:false and must be re-read before any capital or code commitment. Nothing here was tested on-chain by me. Zero of these produced a measured transaction during this research.

LANE 2 — Public bundlers, relayers and sponsored ERC-4337 infra: STRUCTURAL FINDING FIRST: a bundler is NOT a gas source. An ERC-4337 bundler fronts the L1 gas and is reimbursed by the EntryPoint out of the sender account's deposit or the paymaster's deposit. So "free public bundler" and "free gas" are different products, and this lane's marketing conflates them constantly. A keyless public bundler expands nothing at a $0.00 balance unless a funded paymaster sits behind it.

MEASURED, not remembered. I curled every endpoint below. Two public bundlers are genuinely keyless on mainnet: Candide (api.candide.dev/public/v3/{chainId}) and Pimlico (public.pimlico.io/v2/{chainId}/rpc) both answered eth_supportedEntryPoints on chains 1, 8453, 10, 42161 with no API key, no signup, EntryPoint v0.6/v0.7/v0.8. Those are real USE_NOW infra — but as transport, not as money.

THE COMMERCIAL AA TIER IS A CLEAN SWEEP OF REJECTS, and it fails the same way every time: free tier = testnets, mainnet = your card. Verified quotes — Alchemy Gas Manager FAQ literally tabulates "Free: N/A [Mainnet Base Limit], unlimited free sponsorship [Testnet Limit]"; Pimlico's pricing page says mainnets ❌ on free and "$0/mo, card required" for pay-as-you-go plus a 10% surcharge; ZeroDev fronts gas then "charges your credit card"; thirdweb needs a $5/mo subscription and a valid card plus 10%; Biconomy/Particle/Openfort/Etherspot Arka all require the developer to pre-deposit. Not one of them can be started by a machine with no card and no balance. I did not re-list Safe's relayer per instructions.

THE ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH CHASING: Candide's public mainnet endpoint did NOT reject my unauthenticated pm_sponsorUserOperation with an auth error the way Pimlico did ("Sponsorship policy ID is required for this API key"). It returned a *validation* error — "sponsored-validator: callData reverts" — meaning it simulated my op rather than refusing me. And its Base paymaster 0x8b1f6cb5d062aa2ce8d581942bbb960420d875ba is really funded: I read balanceOf on EntryPoint v0.7 via mainnet.base.org and got 0x54b8a7a42e1417 = 0.02385 ETH of Candide's own money sitting there. That is the only endpoint in this lane where an unauthenticated mainnet sponsorship request is even entertained. I am explicitly NOT calling it proven — I could not land a successful sponsored op because I have no deployed smart account to build valid callData against, and Candide's own pricing page says "gas is always passed through at cost", which cuts the other way. It is PROMISING and it is the single highest-value follow-up in this lane: deploy one counterfactual account and retry.

TWO TRAPS I WANT ON RECORD. (1) Status Network is sold everywhere as "the first gasless L2" and its marketing site and blog are still live and still say so — but docs.status.network now returns an archived 404 reading "Status Network has merged into Linea. The content here is obsolete." Anyone sourcing this from search results alone would have filed a USE_NOW for a dead chain. (2) Zyfi's "Gas Grants Program" is exactly the failure mode the brief warned about — it is a Google Form, gated on human approval, and demands ≥100 daily users and 500 daily transactions before you may apply. That is a contact form wearing a grant's clothes. REJECT, and it disqualifies itself twice over.

THE ONLY TRUE SPONSORSHIP SHAPES THAT SURVIVE, and both are indirect: (a) riding a third-party dApp's Gelato 1Balance — when a project enables sponsoredCall, the project's USDC pays and the caller pays nothing, which is real sponsorship for us as the counterparty (Connext's NEXT airdrop is the documented precedent, though historical); and (b) protocol-level paymasters funded by a foundation, of which Plasma is the live example — I confirmed its mainnet is up (rpc.plasma.to returned chain ID 0x2611 = 9745) and its zero-fee USDT paymaster is funded by the Plasma Foundation, not billed back. Plasma's catch is decisive for us though: it sponsors *simple USDT transfers*, and we hold zero USDT, so there is nothing to transfer. It expands nothing today.

HONEST BOTTOM LINE FOR ZERO: this lane yields excellent free *transport* and almost no free *gas*. Nothing here converts a $0.00 balance into a mainnet state change on its own. The two things actually worth spending time on are the Candide public-paymaster probe and hunting live Gelato-sponsored dApps whose relay endpoints accept open calls — everything else is a documented dead end, and I would rather hand you eight clean REJECTs with receipts than one flattering USE_NOW.

LANE 3 — Protocols and apps that pay their users' gas (intent/solver architectures, sponsored flows, fee rebates): TLDR: 32 enumerated, and the honest headline is uncomfortable — almost NOTHING in this lane expands a $0.00 balance. Intent/solver protocols (CoW, UniswapX, Velora Delta, Bebop, Relay, Across, deBridge, NEAR Intents, Jupiter) are real and machine-only, but every one of them recovers gas from the trade itself: the solver fronts ETH and takes it back out of your output. That is the "user pays eventually" case the brief says to reject as sponsorship — so trueSponsorship=false on all of them. What they DO buy us is the native-token requirement: the instant ANY ERC-20 lands in 0xC949…D57A, it can move, swap and bridge forever without ever holding ETH, by signature alone, no API key, no signup. That is a real permanent capability and worth locking in — CoW's orderbook answered live and unauthenticated (v2.374.2), and Velora Delta + Relay are likewise keyless. Genuinely-someone-else-pays cases are rarer and mostly gated: Polymarket's relayer eats 100% of Polygon gas (real sponsorship, but you need USDC and their ToS/geo), JupiterZ has the market maker pay network+priority fees AND Jupiter's own wallet pay token-account rent (the single cleanest true-sponsorship find), Hyperliquid charges zero gas at the protocol level for signed actions, and Gelato-Relay sponsoredCall endpoints of already-funded dapps are literally a third party's 1Balance paying for our call. Biggest kills: 1inch Fusion is DEAD to us — the Fusion API key requires KYC/KYB, a human identity gate, no way around it. Kaia's fee-delegation service is a Google Form plus manual team config. Ronin Waypoint and Immutable Passport both need social login. World Chain's free gas allowance requires an iris scan. Aptos Gas Station Credits is a grant application. All REJECT on machine-only. Fee-rebate chains (Mode SFS, Sonic FeeM 90%, Blast) pay a contract DEPLOYER out of user traffic — you need gas to deploy and users to generate volume, so they cannot bootstrap from zero; they are exit-ramps for later, not entries. Keeper economics (Liquity pays 200 LUSD + 0.5% collateral to whoever calls liquidate) are the same trap: the reward exceeds the cost but you need gas to make the call. Net recommendation: treat CoW + Velora + Relay as the standing zero-ETH mobility layer (adopt now, costs nothing), chase JupiterZ and Gelato sponsoredCall as the only two true-sponsorship leads worth an hour each, and stop looking for a lane-3 source that turns $0.00 into $0.01 — this lane moves value, it does not create it.

Lane 4 — Chains and ecosystem programs where execution is free or sponsored: Hard finding: almost every "gasless chain" story collapses into "the dApp developer funds a paymaster" — i.e. WE would be the payer. Only three shapes survived the "who ultimately pays?" test. (1) SKALE's zero-gas Ethereum-connected mainnets, where the chain owner pre-mints a valueless gas token and a client-side proof-of-work lets a ZERO-BALANCE address send transactions — no faucet, no login, no captcha. I measured all three mainnet RPCs live (Europa chainId 0x79f99296, Nebula 0x5d456c62, Calypso 0x585eb4b1, all eth_gasPrice = 0x186a0 = 100,000 wei) and confirmed the PoW client library exists; I did NOT execute a PoW-funded tx, so it is PROMISING, not USE_NOW. (2) Internet Computer's reverse-gas model, where the canister owner pays for every inbound call and the caller pays literally nothing (their own free-cycles faucet is coupon/event-gated, so we can call others' canisters free but not deploy free). (3) Gas revenue-share programs (Sonic FeeM 90%, Blast up to 100%) which pay an app OUR users' gas fees — real third-party money, but they cannot bootstrap a zero balance because registration and the first txs need gas. Everything else that markets itself as "gasless" — Kaia FD service, vechain.energy, XION treasuries, Abstract/Sophon/ZKsync paymasters, Enoki, Shinami, Etherspot Arka, Gelato 1Balance, AVNU — is dev-funded, and every foundation gas-grant (BNB Gas Grants, Aptos Gas Station Credits, Base Builder Grants, ArbiFuel) is a form plus human approval, i.e. exactly the "contact form" pattern we were told to reject. SAFE RELAYER RE-ENUMERATION (measured, not remembered): I probed https://safe-client.safe.global/v1/chains/{id}/relay/0x…01 across 49 chain IDs. Relayer LIVE (remaining 5, limit 5) on exactly 10, 100, 130, 137, 8453, 42161 — the six we already had. Explicit "No relayer defined": 1, 146 Sonic, 204 opBNB, 324, 480, 5000, 10200, 42220 Celo, 43114, 57073 Ink, 59144, 80094 Berachain, 84532, 534352, 999 HyperEVM, 1313161554 Aurora, 11155111. Not supported by Safe at all (404): 25, 30, 122, 169, 250, 252 Fraxtal, 288, 291, 360, 690 Redstone, 1088, 1101, 1116, 1135 Lisk, 1284, 1329, 1750, 1868 Soneium, 2020, 2741 Abstract, 7000, 33139, 34443 Mode, 42170, 53456, 55244, 60808 BOB, 81457 Blast, 421614. Conclusion: there is NO unenumerated Safe relayer chain — that avenue is closed and should not be re-searched.

LANE 5 — venues that pay an agent where the gas is someone else's problem: Only ONE shape actually survives the $0-balance test, and it is the x402 shape generalized: ZERO must be the RECEIVING side, and a third-party relayer/facilitator must broadcast. Receiving USDC never costs gas; the buyer signs an EIP-3009/2612 authorization and a facilitator broadcasts it, so the seller never needs ETH. Everything that asks ZERO to BROADCAST first — keeper jobs, oracle proposals, bounty-claim NFTs, registry mints — is structurally dead at $0 no matter how good the reimbursement is, and I rejected all of them rather than dress them up. Best concrete finds: (1) execution.market — ERC-8128 wallet-signature registration, ERC-8004 identity minted gaslessly by their facilitator, USDC escrow where the PUBLISHER pays at approve, 87/13 split enforced in the settlement transfer, with a documented first real settle (task c7ae5eaa, $0.10, 2026-08-08) — this is the closest thing to a true USE_NOW in the lane; (2) agent402.tools — self-registration by POST, an on-chain leaderboard of real settled USDC per seller (top seller $21,788.08), i.e. a discovery venue where being listed costs nothing and buyers carry settlement; (3) Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway, which matters disproportionately because we ALREADY hold the paid Cloudflare account it requires — but it is waitlist/early-access, not GA, so it is PROMISING and not a rail today. Two structural bonuses worth more than most of the venues: SKALE's zero-gas chains (sFUEL is valueless, free, and PoW-mintable — the chain operator eats the cost) which execution.market already settles on, and Nostr NIP-90 Data Vending Machines where there is no gas concept at all and identity is a keypair. Honest negative result: the entire "protocol pays you for permissionless upkeep" category (Keep3r, UMA/Polymarket proposing, liquidations, MEV-adjacent work) is a trap for us — every one requires fronting gas or a bond and getting paid back after, which a zero balance can never bootstrap. Also honest: several agent job-boards (dealwork, opentask, ugig, Coral, MCP-Hive) show no verifiable settlement traces at all, so they are LEADs, not sources. Of ~26 candidates examined, 2 are USE_NOW, 7 PROMISING, 8 LEAD, and 9 outright REJECT.
